content.text:
Yes, it has run every week since it was installed. The last run was **Monday 2026-10-19 at 10:06:31**.

**Run history** (from the headers in `~/Library/Logs/package-audit/package-audit.log`):

| Date | Time | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-13 (Sun) | 15:54 | Not a Monday, so probably the run started at install time, by hand or by `audit:agent:run` |
| 2026-09-14 | 10:02 | First scheduled Monday run |
| 2026-09-21 | 10:03 | |
| 2026-09-28 | 10:03 | |
| 2026-10-05 | 10:10 | |
| 2026-10-12 | 10:00 | |
| 2026-10-19 | 10:06 | Latest |

It's now 01:26 on Monday 10-26, so this week's run isn't due until 10:00 this morning. Nothing has been missed.

**What the last run found:** `launchctl` reports `last exit code = 1`. That doesn't mean the job failed. In `script/package-audit`, exit 1 means at least one vulnerability was found, and exit 2 means an auditor itself failed. The 10-19 summary:

- **cargo:** vulnerable (`xplorertui`, 4 advisories)
- **pnpm:** vulnerable (pnpm, ai-cli, firecrawl-cli, chrome-devtools-mcp, cf, …)
- **npm:** vulnerable (`@mem0/cli`, corepack, npm)
- **bun:** vulnerable (codex, pi-coding-agent, elevenlabs cli, agent-browser, typescript, …)
- **uv:** vulnerable (browser-use, hf, llm, trafilatura, ty)
- **yarn:** not installed

The findings include Axios HTTP/2 DoS, undici WebSocket DoS and a PostCSS ReDoS.

`launchctl` also shows `runs = 3`, but the log has 7 runs. That counter only counts runs since the agent was last loaded (after a reboot or reinstall), so the log is the full history. You can print the latest summary again with `mise run audit:log`.

If you want, I can go through the 10-19 findings and sort out which packages just need an upgrade and which are only flagged through a transitive dependency.
